## Problem

Christine and her friends are organizing a movie marathon from her family's extensive film collection. They want to begin with a movie of any runtime and then choose subsequent movies so that each one is either the same length as the movie immediately before it or exactly one minute longer. Opening and closing credits are included in each runtime. No movie may be watched more than once, even if it is not shown consecutively. Popcorn will be provided.

Assuming the marathon is planned to include as many movies as possible, implement the function below to find the maximum number of movies that can be watched while following these rules.

## Function Description

Finish implementing `longestMarathon` in the code editor.

`longestMarathon` accepts the following parameter:

- `int[] runtimes`: an array of integers describing the runtimes of the available movies

## Returns

- `int`: the greatest possible length of a sequence of distinct movies in which every movie after the first has a runtime equal to, or exactly one minute greater than, the preceding movie. Return `0` when no marathon can be formed.

## Constraints

`N/A`

## Example

**Input:** `runtimes = [8, 4, 5, 7, 4]`

**Output:** `3`

The two distinct movies with runtime `4` can be followed by the movie with runtime `5`, producing a valid sequence of three movies.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think about how to turn the problem into finding a longest path in a graph where movies are nodes and edges exist if one movie can follow another (same length or +1 minute) without repeating a movie.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Sort the movies by runtime first, then use dynamic programming: for each movie, the longest chain ending with it is 1 + the longest chain ending with any movie of the same runtime or exactly one minute shorter that appears earlier in the sorted order.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Time complexity O(N log N) from sorting plus O(N) DP if you store best values for each length, but careful: the same length edge also works, so you need to handle both the same and previous length correctly.

</details>
